target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∃ _ : Theory.RE Def9,
    Def3 Def9.theory ∧ Def2 (Def7 Def9) ∧
      (∼Def7 𝗣𝗔) ∈ Def9.theory ∧ ¬ Def2 (∼Def7 𝗣𝗔)
translation: Target is a closed proposition (with no hypotheses or parameters) about a specific arithmetic theory T (Def9). For any recursively enumerable arithmetic theory F, let c(F) (Def7 F) denote the standard arithmetic consistency sentence ¬Prov_{F.craig}(⌜⊥⌝) built from the Δ₁-presented axiom set F.craig obtained from F by Craig's trick (which has the same theorems as F). Let T be the arithmetic theory 𝗣𝗔 ∪ {∼c(𝗣𝗔)}, obtained by adding the formal negation of c(𝗣𝗔) to Peano arithmetic 𝗣𝗔. Target asserts that all five of the following hold simultaneously: (1) the axiom set T is recursively enumerable (providing the condition needed to form c(T)); (2) every theorem of T (every sentence in T.theory, i.e., derivable from T in classical first-order logic) is true in the standard model of arithmetic (the natural numbers); (3) the consistency sentence c(T) is true in the standard model of arithmetic; (4) the sentence ∼c(𝗣𝗔) is a theorem of T (belongs to T.theory); and (5) the sentence ∼c(𝗣𝗔) is not true in the standard model of arithmetic. As written, clause (2) directly contradicts the conjunction of clauses (4) and (5), since it asserts that every theorem of T is true in the natural numbers while clauses (4) and (5) assert that ∼c(𝗣𝗔) is a theorem of T that is not true in the natural numbers.

divergences.description: Instead of asserting that Def9 (PA + ¬Con(PA)) is consistent (which would use Def4, i.e., Entailment.Consistent), Target asserts Def3 Def9.theory, which says that every theorem of Def9 is true in the standard model (∀ σ ∈ Def9.theory, ℕ↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧ σ), i.e., that Def9 is sound. This omits the consistency claim, asserts the very soundness property the counterexample is meant to refute, and directly contradicts the final two conjuncts ((∼Def7 𝗣𝗔) ∈ Def9.theory ∧ ¬ Def2 (∼Def7 𝗣𝗔)), making Target logically false.

judgement.summary: Target is divergent because it uses Def3 Def9.theory (soundness in the standard model) where the claim requires consistency (Def4). This not only fails to match the author's claim, it renders Target self-contradictory and invalid as a counterexample to 'Cons implies Sound'.
